rows: Choose a silhouette for a body type
Start with A-line; it works for nearly every body shape
A-line creates visual balance regardless of proportions — it is the safe default
Create visual elongation
Use monochrome + vertical lines + high waist
Unbroken vertical line + 1/3-2/3 proportion maximizes perceived height
Choose fabric for drape
Start with fiber content + GSM; test bias drape
Weight and fiber determine drape behavior more than visual appearance
Evaluate construction quality
Check inside seams, pattern matching, grain alignment
Interior construction reveals the actual build quality that exterior finish can hide
Decide bespoke vs. MTM vs. RTW
Match to how far the body deviates from standard sizing
Standard bodies → RTW. Moderate variation → MTM. Atypical proportions → bespoke
Select colors for a capsule wardrobe
3 neutrals + 2 accents; all must combine
Combinatorial wardrobe: n pieces that form n*(n-1)/2 outfits requires color coherence
Assess trend longevity
Check if it is a silhouette shift or a detail/color trend
Silhouette shifts last 5-15 years. Color/detail trends last 1-3 seasons
Grade a pattern across sizes
Use non-proportional grading with per-measurement rules
Body proportions change non-linearly across sizes; uniform scaling distorts fit
